snippet: Ten months before facing Carlos Alcaraz in the ATP Finals final, Alexander Zverev lost to him in five sets and 5h27 in the Australian Open semi-finals. On the eve of their rematch in Turin, the world No. 1 explained why that defeat convinced him he was on the right track, as he had predicted that very night.

title: “[Sinner and Alcaraz] are the benchmark”: Zverev’s last chance to beat the best in his year as No. 1
snippet: Year-end No. 1 but winless against Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz in 2026, Alexander Zverev faces the Spaniard in Sunday’s ATP Finals final in Turin with one last chance to beat “the benchmark”, indoors, the only conditions in which he has always had the upper hand against him.

title: Alcaraz and the art of becoming a champion who explores his resources down to the last detail
snippet: Australian Open in January, Paris two weeks ago, a first ATP Finals title within reach: Carlos Alcaraz is filling the gaps in his record, and with a hamstring scare and a serve he has learned to tame, he has used his week in Turin to get to know himself better, ahead of Sunday’s final against Alexander Zverev.

title: 'This is not F1' - Verstappen criticises Las Vegas overtaking frenzy
snippet: The racing in F1’s overtake-filled Las Vegas Grand Prix has split opinion among drivers, with some criticising it as “very artificial” and “not F1”
